claims.text: Reliable formation of noble metal–based HEA nanomaterials is governed by the simultaneous onset of high mixing entropy and minimal atomic-size mismatch.
High mixing entropy and minimal atomic-size mismatch promote formation of a uniform single-phase structure.
A uniform single-phase structure provides homogeneous catalytic active sites.
Varying precursor mixing order and heating profiles can achieve simultaneous nucleation.
Varying precursor mixing order and heating profiles can enhance atomic interdiffusion.
High mixing entropy combined with minimized atomic-size mismatch prevents phase segregation during rapid high-temperature synthesis.
Preventing phase segregation produces a homogeneous distribution of catalytic active sites.
A homogeneous distribution of catalytic active sites governs reliable catalytic performance.
Simultaneous precursor integration will produce a single-phase HEA structure relative to sequential precursor mixing.
Simultaneous precursor integration will enhance catalytic activity relative to sequential precursor mixing.
Simultaneous precursor integration will enhance catalytic stability relative to sequential precursor mixing.
The synthesis temperature must be sufficiently high to overcome diffusion barriers.
The synthesis temperature must remain low enough to prevent extensive sintering.
Atomic-size differences must remain within limits that permit high-entropy stabilization.
Direct experimental evidence linking specific precursor mixing orders to controlled atomic distributions in noble metal–based HEAs is not yet available.
Equivalent phase structure, elemental uniformity, and catalytic performance for simultaneous and sequential mixing would falsify the proposed role of precursor mixing order.
